key_gap: Both sides reached the same leap-with-bounded-commitment, but the human's 80-year-old projection was the spine: performed concretely and argued from Elena's own documents (8 years of letters, mentor testimony, marketability test), it made the omission-vs-commission asymmetry the primary criterion, bracketed the washed-out EV in one move, and pre-eliminated 'wait for more certainty' before it existed. The AI treated the same evidence as a tiebreaker promoted to primary status only at selection, and its own AAR concedes its delay hedge (3-month diligence bridge) was killed only by the 60-day clock at verification — a trace that, had the EV been clearly negative instead of a wash, would have drifted to 'stay' (the status-quo bias the model exists to cut).
learning_signal: For long-horizon career/business commitments where expected value is a wash, the decisive move is a first-class projected-regret pass run BEFORE alternative generation: enumerate alternatives, project each to the horizon (e.g., age 80) and argue the omission-vs-commission asymmetry from the decision-maker's OWN documented values (letters, journals, mentor testimony) rather than generic risk preference; the EV pass must be bracketed as indecisive before the regret test is applied as tiebreaker. Treating the regret asymmetry as a late tiebreaker is fragile: it risks status-quo drift when EV is unfavorable and generates certainty-chasing hedges that a 60-day clock makes fatal.
suggested_improvement: Add a LONG-HORIZON PROJECTION stage to WHAT for commitment decisions (career moves, business bets, relocations): (1) enumerate ≥3 alternatives including delay/defer; (2) project each to the stated horizon and rank by anticipated regret, sourcing the asymmetry from documented values in the evidence, not generic priors; (3) before proceeding, flag any alternative that is status-quo or delay in disguise and require an explicit kill reason; (4) require the EV pass to conclude 'wash or decisive' so the regret test is explicitly the tiebreaker when EV is a wash, and prohibit 'wait for more certainty' hedges unless the calendar allows them.

key_gap: Strict regret minimization amplified the hindsight anchor: the 80-year-old test ratified a $376 purchase after a 47x run as 'a second chance,' converting a vivid 2013 miss into an argument for an all-in $53K position (incl. margin, ~38% of net worth, margin call at ~40% drawdown) with base rates (past 40x+ winners underperforming the index in ~70% of following 5-year windows), valuation (P/E 85 vs. 26), insider sales, and the ruin path excluded from the frame. The AI's blinded run separated the decisions — the 2013 buy at $8 is unavailable in 2026; the available decision is a different one — and delivered a bounded, rule-based conviction slot plus a structural process fix (auto-invest) that treats the emotional state as data about the anchor, not as an allocation input.
learning_signal: The 80-year-old test is an amplifier of whatever regret is currently salient, not a purifier: fed a vivid recent miss it produces emotionally biased, hindsight-contaminated verdicts exactly where sober expected value (base rates, valuation, explicit ruin paths) wins. Before any regret-driven reasoning is allowed to set a decision, a contamination check must run: (1) restate the decision as the one actually available today (a forgone 2013 purchase is not an available 2026 decision); (2) check whether the regret anchors on a prior missed decision or on the forward choice; (3) if contaminated, demote the emotional evidence and require base-rate/valuation evidence to carry the decision; (4) never let leverage (margin) amplify a regret-driven position.
suggested_improvement: Add a REGRET-CONTAMINATION FILTER to the WHY gate, triggered whenever regret-based reasoning appears in the input or in generated content: restate the decision in its current-time form; test for anchor availability ('is the regretted decision still purchasable?'); if the anchor is unavailable, cap emotional evidence and require base rates, valuation, and an explicit worst-case/ruin-path calculation before any allocation; additionally, add a hard rule that margin or leverage may not be introduced into a regret-motivated position without an independent base-rate justification on the record.
